title: The etale compact-support comparisons
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring and use bounded-below complexes of ordinary $\Lambda$-module sheaves on the small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a compactifiable separated finite-type morphism of Noetherian schemes [def-asd-compactifiable], where Noetherian means admitting a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings. Restrict the chosen-compactification candidates of [def-amb-etale-compact-support] to $D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$. The proper-refinement comparisons of [def-weil-pbc-proper-open-comparison] are natural coherent isomorphisms: identities and composites of refinements give identities and composites of comparisons, and comparison through a common refinement is independent of that refinement and satisfies the cocycle condition. Thus these candidates are canonically identified, denoted $Rf_!$. For composable compactifiable separated finite-type morphisms $X\xrightarrow{f}Y\xrightarrow{g}S$ of Noetherian schemes, these identifications give a natural composition isomorphism $Rg_!Rf_!\cong R(gf)_!$ on $D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$, independent of compactification choices and associative for three such morphisms.

proof.text: Apply the normalization clause of thm-cbc-finite-torsion (the second conjunct of compactSupportFiniteTorsion) to the identity Cartesian base-change square with horizontal identities and vertical morphism f, and then to d, the arbitrary refinement r : c.Refinement d, and K. This identifies compactSupportProperOpenRefinementMap with the hom component of (derivedPlusFormalism (ModuleCat Λ)).shriekIso d c. No Noetherian, Cartesian-refinement or density hypothesis is added.

Use the existing bounded-below compactification comparison family: rightDerivedLowerShriekOfCompactificationPlusRefinementIso_eq identifies the refinement isomorphism with (PlusIso c d).symm; PlusIso_symm identifies this with PlusIso d c; derivedPlusFormalism_shriekIso identifies the formalism comparison with PlusIso d c. These are equalities of the already constructed canonical comparisons, evaluated at K. The existing refinement identity/composition and cocycle declarations recorded on this node continue to supply those clauses, and the unchanged public LowerShriekComposition import supplies the already constructed choice-independent associative composition package.

Unfold compactSupportProperOpenRefinementMap only in the normalization equality. Before comparing morphisms, rewrite its pushforward compositor and the theorem goal with the already proved derivedPlusFormalism_pfComp'_inv. Thus both sides use the identical canonical derived-functor compositor, avoiding computation of the formalism's adjunction-based compositor. Rewrite the two comparison identities of the preceding step and finish by symmetry of the normalization equality. This is elementary rewriting of existing API equalities; it introduces no auxiliary mathematical obligation.
